chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The daughters of the daughter stand in the place of the daughter when there are no daughters for the deceased and no other heir besides them; and the daughters of the son stand in the place of the son when there is no son for the deceased and no other heir besides them.

key_terms.بَنَاتُ الِابْنَةِ: Daughters of the daughter (granddaughters via daughter)
key_terms.بَنَاتُ الِابْنِ: Daughters of the son (granddaughters via son)
key_terms.يَقُمْنَ مَقَامَ: Stand in the place of / represent

ai.seo_question: How do granddaughters inherit in Shia Islamic law when there are no direct children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia principle of 'al-awla bi-l-ba'in' (the closer branch takes precedence) by establishing that granddaughters through a daughter inherit as daughters in the absence of other daughters or heirs, while granddaughters through a son inherit as sons when there are no sons or other heirs. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia approach to grandchild inheritance, where the line of descent through the son is prioritized over that through the daughter, contrasting with the Sunni practice of 'rad' or exclusion in certain scenarios. The narration underscores the importance of specific heir categories in determining the distribution of the estate according to the Quranic shares.
